newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway oil union, employers to hold mediated talks.
newsitem.headline: Norway oil union, employers to hold mediated talks.

text.p: The Federation of Norwegian Oil Workers (OFS) said on Monday it would begin state- mediated talks with Norwegian shipowners in August to try and avert a strike on floating production installations.

Bjoern Tjessem, OFS first deputy, said the union served a warning of industrial action to the shipowners association (NR) and the state mediator last Wednesday. The strike is due to begin on August 23.
OFS has 800 members on 20 floating systems on the Norwegian continental shelf. Tjessem said it was unclear if the action, if it goes ahead, would immediately affect oil production.
However, prolonged action could result in the shutdown of some oil and gas production and also would affect exploration and drilling activity and other support functions.
"The state mediator has informed us that we are required to hold mediated negotiations in Oslo somewhere between August 18 and 20," Tjessem told Reuters.
"Of course we hope to come to an agreement during the mediated negotiations, but if it is necessary we are ready to do it (strike)."

Talks between OFS and NR broke down at the end of June. The dispute centres on a rise in the minimum wage for managers with individual salary agreements, completion of a harmonisation in terms covering workers on fixed and floating installations, and pension terms.
Unions are required by Norwegian law to inform employers and the state mediator of intended industrial action. All parties then begin a period of mediated talks with a deadline.
If no solution is agreed in those talks then unions are free to strike as soon as the deadline has passed.
